stop_condition: the ERROR:TOOL-FAILURE sentinel emitted by the detector functions in design-structural.test.sh is handled at EVERY consumer site (no site coerces it into an ordinary value via string comparison, arithmetic, test -gt, a case without a sentinel arm, or an unquoted expansion); the rc-capture sites correctly treat grep rc=1 as NO MATCH rather than as a tool failure, and only rc>1 as a real failure; and round 3's own fix introduces no new instance of the same defect

findings.location: review scope and provenance for this artifact; .claude/scripts/tests/design-structural.test.sh
findings.evidence:
VERDICT AS RETURNED: the sentinel is handled at every consumer site; no unhandled consumer remains. The reviewer enumerated eight consumer-site groups and classified each as handled: :591 (strip_line_comments gated on rc != 0); :629,:636,:672 (sub-detector outputs gated by return status before arithmetic); :715-716,:762-768,:785-787 (raw results to assert_eq, where the sentinel cannot equal an expected numeric count and so fails loudly); :848-865 (the explicit three-way case with a sentinel arm, which is round 3's R3-F1a fix); :921-941 and :1042-1048 (compared raw against expected "0"); :1055-1057 (explicitly EXPECTS the sentinel); and :810-818 plus :1027-1034 (direct grep checks that synthesize the sentinel on rc>1, then compare raw against "0"). Both secondary checks returned clean: rc=1 is treated as no-match and only rc>1 as tool failure at both capture sites, and this round's changes introduce no new instance of the defect.

NOT TAKEN ON TRUST. Two of the cited ranges were spot-checked against the file by the orchestrator before this artifact was written, because a fast, confidently-formatted review is exactly the shape a confabulated one takes. :810-818 is precisely the described shape (grep -cE, rc capture, `[ "$BOUNDARY_NONLINEAR_RC" -gt 1 ]` -> sentinel, else empty-coerced to 0, then assert_eq against "0"), and :1053-1058 does assert TOOL_FAILURE_SENTINEL as the EXPECTED value on an unreadable path. The reviewer read the source; the enumeration is not fabricated.

SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW, STATED SO THE APPROVAL DOES NOT OVERCLAIM. This round reviewed ONE file, .claude/scripts/tests/design-structural.test.sh, against ONE question, by explicit instruction. It did NOT review the ~1,500 lines of test scaffolding elsewhere in the change set, workflow-doctor.sh, the release documentation, or the LIVE-1 record. Rounds 1-3 (which found HIGH+HIGH, then HIGH+MED, then HIGH+MED+LOW) covered the production function and the two new specs. Nothing in this change set has had an independent review of the documentation edits.

MODEL IDENTIFICATION CAVEAT. reviewer_pin is read from ~/.codex/config.toml (`model = "gpt-5.6-sol"`, model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"). reviewer_model is supposed to be a RUNTIME SELF-REPORT (review-check.sh:493) rather than a restatement of the pin. Asked directly, the reviewer answered: "I'm Codex, powered by GPT-5; my exact runtime model identifier isn't exposed to me." So reviewer_model records the self-reported family, gpt-5, and NOT the pin value; the exact runtime identifier is genuinely unavailable rather than omitted. Recording the limitation instead of silently copying the pin across, which would have made the two fields falsely corroborate each other.

RELAY NOTE. This round was first dispatched as an inlined-content request and hung for 1h16m30s with no return before being killed. The identical review question, re-asked as a ~2KB pointer-style prompt that let the reviewer read the file itself, returned in roughly two minutes. See claude-workflow-plugin-3o4r / -on63; the packet-size hypothesis is NOT established by this episode (the hung packet's byte size was never measured and is no longer recoverable), but pointer-style requests are the cheap workaround regardless of mechanism.
findings.description: No action requested. Recorded as info so the approval carries what this review did and did not cover, the provenance of the two model fields, and the relay behaviour, rather than leaving an unqualified 'approve' to imply broader coverage than four rounds against one question actually provide.
